hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are buzzing with optimism after a 2-1 victory over Chelsea, with Odegaard's carbon-copy goal and Konsa's dominant defensive debut earning praise. There's a growing belief that Arsenal can build a substantial lead before Christmas given unconvincing performances from Chelsea, Liverpool, and City. The mood is confident and title-believing, though some grumbles about the inconvenient 8pm Sunderland kickoff and kit similarities punctuate the otherwise buoyant atmosphere.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment shifted dramatically across the day, rising from nervy pre-match caution (6/10) through half-time anxiety to electrifying post-match triumph (9/10) after a 2-1 comeback derby win over Chelsea. The narrative arc moved from familiar 'don't bottle it' dread to emphatic 'men against boys' title-champion energy, with Odegaard and Havertz's heroics silencing early-season doubts. Minor fatigue grumbles aside, the day closed with the machine firmly in top gear and title talk fully reignited.

weekly.summary: The week began with mounting frustration over the club's failure to land a marquee attacking signing on deadline day, sending sentiment to a low around September 1st (4/10). However, mood steadily recovered through the back half of the week as defensive solidity, gritty wins, and growing anticipation for the Chelsea derby lifted fans, culminating in a triumphant 8/10 after a dramatic 2-1 comeback victory. The dominant arc is clearly upward—from transfer-window despair to title-champion euphoria—anchored by resilience, defensive strength, and a reignited belief in the squad.
